title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 317: The Tragedy of the Commons and Ocean Quotas
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 317 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Tragedy of the Commons: Oceanic Depletion and Quotas

Paragraph 1. In 1968, scientist Garrett Hardin wrote a famous article called 'The Tragedy of the Commons'. He studied shared natural places that nobody owns, such as open oceans or public grass fields. Hardin showed that if every person tries to take as much as possible for personal profit, the shared resource is destroyed. For example, each farmer adds one extra cow to gain more money, until all the grass disappears and everyone loses.

Paragraph 2. Today, this same problem is hurting the world's oceans. Over the past fifty years, huge fishing ships with fish-finders and deep nets have caught way too many fish. A United Nations report warns that more than one-third of world fish populations are now in danger. To solve this problem, governments created Individual Transferable Quotas (ITQs). Under this rule, the government sets a total fish limit and gives fishing shares to companies, which can buy or sell them.

Paragraph 3. However, researcher Dr. Clara Mercer warns that ITQs did not save the oceans cleanly. Instead of helping small local fishers, rich corporations and big investment funds bought most of the fishing shares. As a result, a few huge companies now control nearly all fishing rights.

Paragraph 4. Worse still, quotas create a wasteful habit called 'high-grading'. Because companies only want the highest price for their limited fish share, ship workers throw smaller dead fish back into the ocean and keep only the biggest, most expensive fish. Dr. Mercer concludes that selling ocean shares has not fixed the problem of overfishing.

groups.title: Questions 1–4
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

q1.text: What did Garrett Hardin warn happens to shared resources that nobody owns?
options: A. People work together peacefully to protect them.
B. Individual greed eventually destroys the shared resource.
C. Governments immediately close them to all workers.

steps: Đoạn 1: Nếu mỗi người đều cố lấy nhiều nhất cho lợi ích cá nhân thì tài nguyên chung sẽ bị hủy hoại.

q2.text: What is the main idea behind Individual Transferable Quotas (ITQs)?
options: A. Banning all fishing boats from deep ocean areas
B. Paying fishers to stop eating seafood for five years
C. Dividing a total fish limit into shares companies can trade

steps: Đoạn 2: Chính phủ đặt tổng hạn mức và chia thành các suất có thể mua bán.

q3.text: According to Dr. Clara Mercer, who gained the most fishing shares under ITQs?
options: A. Rich corporations and big investment funds

steps: Đoạn 3: Các tập đoàn giàu có và quỹ đầu tư lớn đã mua lại phần lớn hạn ngạch.

q4.text: What happens during 'high-grading' on fishing ships?
options: A. Fishers save small fish inside special tanks to grow bigger.
B. Workers throw smaller dead fish overboard and keep only top-value fish.
C. Captains donate extra fish to local food charities.

steps: Đoạn 4: Ném bỏ cá nhỏ đã chết xuống biển để giữ phần hạn ngạch cho cá to đắt tiền.

q5.text: The United Nations plans to replace all big trawlers with wooden boats next year.

steps: Đoạn 2: Liên Hợp Quốc chỉ cảnh báo hơn 1/3 nguồn cá gặp nguy hiểm, không nói chuyện thay tàu gỗ.

q6.text: Modern fishing ships with fish-finders have reduced fish numbers over the last 50 years.

steps: Đoạn 2: "Over the past fifty years, huge fishing ships with fish-finders... caught way too many fish."

q7.text: Small local fishers became much richer after ITQs were introduced.

steps: Đoạn 3: Tập đoàn lớn mua hết hạn ngạch, không phải ngư dân nhỏ giàu lên.

q8.text: Under high-grading, crews carefully keep every single small fish they catch.

steps: Đoạn 4: Họ ném bỏ cá nhỏ đã chết xuống biển (throw smaller dead fish back), không giữ lại hết.
